name: Ethylestrenol (Maxibolin)

lead: Ethylestrenol (Maxibolin, Orabolin) is an oral nandrolone-derived anabolic steroid first described in 1959 and approved in the US in 1964. It was prescribed to promote weight and muscle gain, in catabolic states, and for some anemias and bone conditions; bodybuilders have used it for lean, low-water gains.

It is an androgen receptor agonist with strong progestogenic activity and a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio, considered a prodrug of norethandrolone, with receptor affinity about 5 percent of testosterone's according to Wikipedia. Wikipedia describes it as a very weak muscle-builder, so it has not been commonly used for physique. It is no longer used in humans and appears to survive only as a veterinary product in a few countries. No appearance trials were found.

paras: It was taken orally as a medicine. Physique use has been uncommon and is based on discussion rather than documented routines.

Reported effects include virilization (acne, hirsutism, voice changes) and possible liver damage as a 17α-alkylated steroid. Pregnancy and prostate cancer are contraindications. It is Schedule III in the US and Schedule IV in Canada.

angle.text: Ethylestrenol was used for lean, low-water mass gains: as an oral nandrolone derivative it activates androgen receptors with a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio. It was studied medically for wasting and anemia, and Wikipedia describes it as a weak muscle-builder.

lead: Ethylestrenol (also ethyloestrenol; brand names Maxibolin and Orabolin) is a synthetic oral androgen and anabolic steroid with progestogenic activity, derived from nandrolone by 17α-alkylation. It was first described in 1959, approved for medical use in 1961, and approved in the United States in 1964. [1]

Historically it was prescribed to promote weight gain and muscle growth, for catabolic states such as corticosteroid therapy, chronic infection, surgery and trauma, for treatment-refractory anemias, as an adjunct in osteoporosis and for short stature in young people. It is no longer used in humans and appears to be available only for veterinary use in Australia and New Zealand. [1]

Wikipedia says it has been used to improve physique and performance but is a very weak muscle-builder compared with other anabolic steroids, so it has not been commonly used for that purpose. No trials of it for appearance outcomes were found. [1]

paras: Ethylestrenol was prescribed for weight gain and muscle growth, for catabolic states, for refractory anemias, for arthritis and for short stature in youth. [1]

Case reports and small series used it in vascular conditions. Delta-4-ethylestrenol was reported in recurrent deep venous thrombosis, and it was one of the fibrinolytic agents tried in Degos disease and in atrophie blanche, a livedo vasculitis. [2][3][4]

Ethylestrenol is an androgen receptor agonist with strong progestogenic activity and low estrogenic activity after conversion. It is metabolized to norethandrolone and is therefore a prodrug. Its affinity for the androgen receptor is very low and its affinity for sex hormone-binding globulin is also very low. [1] A comparative binding study of anabolic steroids to androgen receptors in rat and rabbit muscle and prostate is one of the standard references for this class. [5]

Virilization, including acne, hirsutism, voice changes and increased libido, has been reported, along with possible liver damage typical of 17α-alkylated steroids. Pregnancy is a contraindication because of the risk of masculinizing a female fetus, and prostate cancer is a contraindication because it may accelerate progression. [1]

Wikipedia lists the US status as Schedule III, Canada as Schedule IV and Brazil as Class C5, and says non-medical use is generally illicit. Veterinary brands include Nandoral, Nitrotain and Oestrotain. [1] Analytical studies have examined metabolites in cattle feces and in greyhounds as markers of illicit use in animals. [6][7] A trout growth study tested it as a growth promoter in fish diets. [8]
A 1995 rat study reported that ethylestrenol, like pregnenolone sulfate, affected retention of a passive avoidance task. This was animal behavior research, not an appearance study. [9]
No studies found of ethylestrenol for muscle or appearance outcomes. Human literature consists of older case reports in vascular and skin conditions. [2][3][4]
